touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
Instance: every device has at least one; a singleton is instance 0.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
Logging and diagnostics, including diagnostic_inspector: the smart reader of the dumb breadcrumbs base's logging leaves; complete diagnosis on the first pass.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
